purpose: Machine-readable form of ROADMAP.md's ordered steps, read by tools/roadmap.mjs. The `state` on every record is a CLAIM copied from the prose; the tool verifies it against `evidence` at run time and downgrades an unverifiable claim to UNVERIFIED rather than trusting this file. Do not hand-edit `state` without also updating the evidence that justifies it — that is the exact drift this file exists to catch.
note_on_evidence: Each evidence entry proves the state CURRENTLY claimed, not the step's eventual closes_when. A `path` entry must exist on disk. A `command` entry must exit with the stated code (default 0) and, if `contains` is given, its combined stdout+stderr must contain that substring. A `json_field` entry reads a JSON file and checks a top-level key against `one_of`. All commands here are offline, no browser, no GPU pod, and each was timed under 2s when this file was written.

steps.title: Surfaces respond to light
steps.visible_outcome: Stone reads as stone, wood as wood, leather as leather. Objects sit on the ground instead of floating on it. Shadowed areas have detail in them instead of being black.
steps.closes_when: Protocol A is re-run blind against the same plates and we stop losing 5 of 5. Not when the orphan count reaches zero — statistics can fail a build and can never pass one.

evidence.note: the blind round that lost 5 of 5 and set FIDELITY's cap at 5 against a gate of 7.0 — the baseline this step must move
sub-step (a), the diagnosed defect, is at least started
one of the fix's landing sites

steps.unevidenced_note: closes_when needs a REPEAT of Protocol A (a fresh blind-judgement verdict at corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/W1-VISUAL-BLIND-PROTOCOL-A-r2.json or later) that clears the pass threshold. That file does not exist yet, so this step cannot read as done no matter what evidence sub-steps (a)-(c) accumulate — recorded here rather than invented as a proxy metric.

substeps.title: Bind the material set — the orphan fix
substeps.visible_outcome: The player's body and every affected surface (305 of 406 materials) actually run the surface shader whose uniforms they already carry, instead of the uniforms sitting unread in userData.
substeps.closes_when: The CONSUMPTION arms (before/after) are filed and a hardware before/after sweep, both arms on the same Pod and the same GPU, confirms the orphan count went 305 to 0 and the rendered pixels differ.

evidence.note: diagnosed, fixed and landed at the code seam; hardware CONSUMPTION evidence explicitly still open per this file's own could_not_do list
the census instrument the 305/406 figure was measured with
the fix, at the copy seam

substeps.title: Contact shadows and ambient occlusion
substeps.visible_outcome: Objects sit on the ground instead of floating on it — the defect judges named 5 of 5, the most universal finding in the blind round.
substeps.closes_when: A contact-shadow or AO term is present in the render path (not just declared in FEATURE_CONSUMERS) and a before/after capture shows darkening at contact points that was not there before.

substeps.title: Ambient/GI fill with tone-mapped shadow lift
substeps.visible_outcome: Shadowed areas have detail in them instead of being crushed to black.
substeps.closes_when: An ambient/GI fill term is present in the render path and a before/after capture shows detail recoverable in a previously-black shadow region.

steps.title: The first five minutes look and behave right
steps.visible_outcome: You come out of character creation in Thorn, facing somewhere sensible, in a town that looks like a Black Marsh tidewater settlement, and you can walk out of the door without being inside another building.
steps.closes_when: A hardware capture of the real opening path, many angles plus motion, looks right to a person.

evidence.note: door exits set facing across all 115 interiors; the facing rule that fixes the doorstep is offline-measured but not yet browser-swept
Thorn gained roof.needle and a Tidewrack landing built from reused parts
the offline cross-validated instrument the facing numbers came from

steps.unevidenced_note: closes_when is a human-judgement condition ('looks right to a person') with no filed verdict yet — ROADMAP.md itself says the capture daemon returned zero frames under load, so 'nobody has looked at any of the Thorn work'. Evidence for DONE should be a blind-judgement or capture-review verdict naming this step; none exists on disk, so this cannot be marked done by any mechanical proxy.

steps.title: Buildings are not inside each other
steps.visible_outcome: Doors open into streets rather than into other buildings.
steps.closes_when: The 83 interpenetrating pairs across 8 of 8 settlements are resolved by fixing the axis-aligned-vs-rotated comparison defect in the shrink pass and _deepOverlaps(), with 72 of 83 separating without moving a building.

evidence.note: the census that found 83 pairs, 63 invisible to the shipped axis-aligned check
the resolver is built and is itself waiting on an independent critic — not self-graded (rule 22)
the standing gate: NO SETTLEMENT MAY GROW A NEW BUILDING-INSIDE-A-BUILDING

steps.visible_outcome: Asking about one topic opens others, so a conversation branches outward instead of being a flat list; speakers disagree with each other; and the window looks like Morrowind's.
steps.closes_when: Topic visibility and reachability rise substantially past their current measured floors (22% -> 50% and climbing across landed batches; ten topics reachable from no greeting; 100 of 865 npc.topics entries name nothing; 52-61% of NPCs advertise no subject of their own) and the dialogue window matches the vendored Morrowind screenshot REF-A12c.

steps.title: Combat feel
steps.visible_outcome: Fights that feel like Souls — readable animation, weight, a difficulty curve worth climbing, and a moment-to-moment feel worth repeating.
steps.closes_when: Human judges actually fight the game (not view charts of enemy behaviour) and rate the animation, difficulty and feel — named explicitly by the owner as its own step, not a background property.

evidence.note: round 3 AI work (closing on a fleeing player, spacing loop) is built; round 2's own critic verdict FAILed at 2/10 on the spacing-loop gate, so round 3 exists specifically to answer that failure and has no filed critic verdict of its own yet
the round-2 critic verdict: FAIL, overall 2/10, min-aggregated on E_spacing_loop_M3 — recorded so this step cannot quietly read as further along than a fresh critic has actually confirmed
the standing content-integrity gate for game/data/combat/ai.json

steps.unevidenced_note: closes_when's human half — 'how good the combat is ... how fun it feels' — has no filed verdict and, per ROADMAP.md, no judge has yet been asked to fight anything rather than view a chart. No mechanical proxy is substituted here; a blind play-judgement verdict naming this step is the only evidence that should ever mark it done.
